title: Introduce symbolic sparsity injector and interactive latency combiner
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: We frequently observe tail latency regressions tied to pathological sparsity patterns that only appear when quantized kernels and small interactive batches intersect. This PR introduces two benchmarking primitives to make these cases reproducible and measurable in the benchmark-lab suite: a symbolic sparsity injector to synthesize realistic sparse weight/activation maps and an interactive latency combiner that merges short, interleaved traces into per-kernel alignment metrics suitable for p95/p99 attribution.

Summary: Adds a simulation harness (benchmarks/sparsity_injector) and a reporting pipeline (reporting/interactive_combiner) plus an end-to-end e2e test that runs a small model trace with injected sparsity and emits a combined latency breakdown. The injector supports multiple sparsity modes (block, stripe, random-biased) and a seed-based generator so runs are deterministic for CI. The combiner aligns kernel invocation timestamps across interleaved sessions and produces an output artifact compatible with the existing flame-serializer used by the dashboard.

What changed (high-level):
- New binary: benchmark-lab/bin/sparsity-injector (go) - produces synthetic model checkpoints and lightweight kernel-call traces.
- New library: benchmark-lab/benchmarks/sparsity_injector - generator, profiles, and mode definitions.
- New pipeline: benchmark-lab/reporting/interactive_combiner - script (py) that ingests multiple short traces and outputs aligned per-kernel metrics and a combined JSON summary.
- e2e test: benchmark-lab/integration/sparsity_integration_test.py - runs injector + combiner, asserts deterministic p95/p99 in a CI-friendly sample size.
- CI: added a lightweight job entry to .github/workflows/benchmarks.yml to run the new e2e test under the fast-perf label.

Testing and results: Ran local perf runs on a small a2-like instance. Representative results: with random-biased sparsity (30% effective sparsity) the combiner shows a kernel-level p95 delta of +12ms on the quantized matmul hotpath vs the dense baseline; block sparsity shows less delta but increases variance. The e2e test asserts that combined artifact schema and deterministic seed produce identical summaries across repeated runs.

Backward compatibility: No changes to production runtime. All artifacts live under benchmark-lab and are opt-in for CI. The output schema is intentionally backward-compatible with the flame-serializer (adds optional fields: sparsity_mode, sparsity_seed, injection_map_ref).

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc reviewed internally (ENG-4521)
- [x] Unit tests for generator and combiner
- [x] E2E integration test added and wired into fast-perf CI job
- [x] Benchmarks run and sample artifacts attached to the PR

Usage notes: The injector accepts --mode, --seed, --sparsity-pct, and outputs a small tarball with checkpoints and trace.json. The combiner accepts multiple trace.json files and a --session-map to indicate interleaving order; defaults are provided for the e2e test.

Follow-ups: 1) Add a stratified checker that validates whether a runtime's kernel selection changes when presented with injected sparsity; planned as ENG-4587. 2) Add a runner that feeds these artifacts into the canary harness used by perf-canary for automated regression detection.

Attachments: linked artifacts (artifact IDs in CI run), sample combined JSON (see bench-results/531210-summary.json).
